                let _ = socket.send(Message::Close(Some(CloseFrame { code: 1001, reason: Utf8Bytes::from_static("server stopped") }))).await;

//! Per-session token (128 bits from the OS random source) and a constant-time compare.

use ring::rand::{SecureRandom, SystemRandom};

/// 16 random bytes as 32 lowercase hex characters, or `None` if the OS source fails.
pub fn generate() -> Option<String> {
    let mut b = [0u8; 16];
    SystemRandom::new().fill(&mut b).ok()?;
    Some(hex(&b))
}

pub fn hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    const DIGITS: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";
    let mut s = String::with_capacity(bytes.len() * 2);
    for b in bytes {
        s.push(DIGITS[usize::from(b >> 4)] as char);
        s.push(DIGITS[usize::from(b & 15)] as char);
    }
    s
}

/// Equality without an early exit: the loop always covers the longer input,
/// and a length difference is folded into the result, not branched on.
pub fn ct_eq(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {
    let n = a.len().max(b.len());
    let mut diff = a.len() ^ b.len();
    for i in 0..n {
        let x = a.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(0);
        let y = b.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(0);
        diff |= usize::from(x ^ y);
    }
    std::hint::black_box(diff) == 0
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::rng::SplitMix64;

    #[test]
    fn token_is_32_hex_and_differs() {
        let a = generate().unwrap();
        let b = generate().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a.len(), 32);
        assert!(a.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || (b'a'..=b'f').contains(&c)));
        assert_ne!(a, b);
    }

    /// L2: `ct_eq` agrees with `==` for random inputs, including prefixes and different lengths.
    #[test]
    fn l2_ct_eq_matches_equality() {
        let mut rng = SplitMix64::new(0x1A2B);
        for _ in 0..500 {
            let la = rng.below(40) as usize;
            let a: Vec<u8> = (0..la).map(|_| rng.below(4) as u8).collect();
            let b: Vec<u8> = match rng.below(4) {
                0 => a.clone(),
                1 => a.iter().copied().chain([0u8]).collect(),
                2 => a.iter().copied().take(la / 2).collect(),
                _ => (0..rng.below(40) as usize).map(|_| rng.below(4) as u8).collect(),
            };
            assert_eq!(ct_eq(&a, &b), a == b, "{a:?} vs {b:?}");
        }
        assert!(ct_eq(b"", b""));
        assert!(!ct_eq(b"", b"\0"));
    }
}

//! Interface choice and bind rules for the LAN dashboard (R22, safety rule 15).
//!
//! Only private IPv4 addresses are ever offered or accepted. `0.0.0.0`, public,
//! link-local, multicast and IPv6 addresses are refused. Loopback is accepted
//! only when the caller opts in (tests and the e2e build); it is never listed.

use qrcode::{Color, QrCode};
use serde::Serialize;
use std::net::{IpAddr, Ipv4Addr, SocketAddr};
use thiserror::Error;

pub const DEFAULT_PORT: u16 = 8443;
pub const MIN_PORT: u16 = 1024;

#[derive(Debug, Error, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BindError {
    #[error("only private IPv4 addresses (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x) can be shared")]
    NotPrivate,
    #[error("port must be between {MIN_PORT} and 65535")]
    BadPort,
}

/// One selectable interface address.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct Interface {
    pub name: String,
    pub ip: Ipv4Addr,
}

/// True for the RFC 1918 ranges.
pub fn is_private_v4(ip: Ipv4Addr) -> bool {
    ip.is_private()
}

/// Validate the address and port the user picked.
pub fn check_bind(ip: IpAddr, port: u16, allow_loopback: bool) -> Result<SocketAddr, BindError> {
    let IpAddr::V4(v4) = ip else {
        return Err(BindError::NotPrivate);
    };
    let ok = is_private_v4(v4) || (allow_loopback && v4.is_loopback());
    if !ok || v4.is_unspecified() || v4.is_multicast() || v4.is_broadcast() {
        return Err(BindError::NotPrivate);
    }
    // Port 0 (ephemeral) exists for tests, behind the same opt-in as loopback.
    if port < MIN_PORT && !(allow_loopback && port == 0) {
        return Err(BindError::BadPort);
    }
    Ok(SocketAddr::new(ip, port))
}

/// Private IPv4 addresses of this machine, sorted by name then address.
pub fn private_interfaces() -> Vec<Interface> {
    let mut out: Vec<Interface> = if_addrs::get_if_addrs()
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|i| match i.ip() {
            IpAddr::V4(v4) if is_private_v4(v4) && !i.is_loopback() => Some(Interface { name: i.name, ip: v4 }),
            _ => None,
        })
        .collect();
    out.sort_by(|a, b| (&a.name, a.ip).cmp(&(&b.name, b.ip)));
    out.dedup();
    out
}

/// A QR code as rows of `'1'` (dark) and `'0'` (light), without quiet zone.
/// The UI draws it on a canvas; no HTML or SVG string is produced.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct QrMatrix {
    pub size: usize,
    pub rows: Vec<String>,
}

pub fn qr_matrix(text: &str) -> Option<QrMatrix> {
    let code = QrCode::new(text.as_bytes()).ok()?;
    let size = code.width();
    let colors = code.to_colors();
    let rows = colors
        .chunks(size)
        .map(|row| row.iter().map(|c| if *c == Color::Dark { '1' } else { '0' }).collect())
        .collect();
    Some(QrMatrix { size, rows })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::testkit::check;

    /// L7: only RFC 1918 (and loopback on request) binds; nothing else, ever.
    #[test]
    fn l7_bind_accepts_exactly_private_ranges() {
        check("l7_bind", 500, |rng| {
            let ip = Ipv4Addr::from(rng.next_u32());
            let port = 1024 + rng.below(60_000) as u16;
            let private = ip.octets()[0] == 10
                || (ip.octets()[0] == 172 && (16..=31).contains(&ip.octets()[1]))
                || (ip.octets()[0] == 192 && ip.octets()[1] == 168);
            assert_eq!(check_bind(IpAddr::V4(ip), port, false).is_ok(), private, "{ip}");
            let with_loop = check_bind(IpAddr::V4(ip), port, true).is_ok();
            assert_eq!(with_loop, private || ip.is_loopback(), "{ip}");
        });
    }

    #[test]
    fn refuses_unspecified_v6_and_low_ports() {
        let any = IpAddr::from([0, 0, 0, 0]);
        assert_eq!(check_bind(any, 8443, true), Err(BindError::NotPrivate));
        assert_eq!(check_bind(any, 8443, false), Err(BindError::NotPrivate));
        assert_eq!(
            check_bind(IpAddr::from([0u16; 8]), 8443, true),
            Err(BindError::NotPrivate)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            check_bind(IpAddr::from([239, 1, 1, 1]), 8443, true),
            Err(BindError::NotPrivate)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            check_bind(IpAddr::from([169, 254, 1, 1]), 8443, true),
            Err(BindError::NotPrivate)
        );
        let lan = IpAddr::from([192, 168, 1, 5]);
        assert_eq!(check_bind(lan, 80, false), Err(BindError::BadPort));
        assert_eq!(check_bind(lan, 0, false), Err(BindError::BadPort));
        assert!(check_bind(lan, DEFAULT_PORT, false).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn listed_interfaces_are_private_and_not_loopback() {
        for i in private_interfaces() {
            assert!(is_private_v4(i.ip) && !i.ip.is_loopback());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn qr_matrix_is_square_and_binary() {
        let q = qr_matrix("https://192.168.1.5:8443/?t=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(q.rows.len(), q.size);
        assert!(
            q.rows
                .iter()
                .all(|r| r.len() == q.size && r.bytes().all(|c| c == b'0' || c == b'1'))
        );
    }
}

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::net::IpAddr;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct LimitConfig {

    pub capacity: f64,
    /// Requests per second added back.
    pub refill_per_s: f64,
    /// Failed token checks in `fail_window_ms` that trigger a lockout.
    pub fail_limit: usize,
    pub fail_window_ms: i64,
    pub lockout_ms: i64,
    /// Addresses remembered; the least recently seen is dropped beyond this.
    pub max_addrs: usize,
}

impl Default for LimitConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            capacity: 60.0,
            refill_per_s: 30.0,
            fail_limit: 5,
            fail_window_ms: 60_000,
            lockout_ms: 60_000,
            max_addrs: 1024,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Verdict {
    Allow,
    Limited { retry_after_s: u64 },
}

#[derive(Debug)]
struct Entry {
    tokens: f64,
    last_ms: i64,
    fails: Vec<i64>,
    locked_until: i64,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Limiter {
    cfg: LimitConfig,
    map: HashMap<IpAddr, Entry>,
}

impl Limiter {
    pub fn new(cfg: LimitConfig) -> Self {
        Self {
            cfg,
            map: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn tracked(&self) -> usize {
        self.map.len()
    }

    fn entry(&mut self, ip: IpAddr, now: i64) -> &mut Entry {
        if !self.map.contains_key(&ip) && self.map.len() >= self.cfg.max_addrs.max(1) {
            let oldest = self.map.iter().min_by_key(|(_, e)| e.last_ms).map(|(k, _)| *k);
            if let Some(k) = oldest {
                self.map.remove(&k);
            }
        }
        let capacity = self.cfg.capacity;
        self.map.entry(ip).or_insert(Entry {
            tokens: capacity,
            last_ms: now,
            fails: Vec::new(),
            locked_until: i64::MIN,
        })
    }

    /// Take one request from the address's bucket.
    pub fn check(&mut self, ip: IpAddr, now_ms: i64) -> Verdict {
        let (capacity, refill) = (self.cfg.capacity, self.cfg.refill_per_s);
        let e = self.entry(ip, now_ms);
        if now_ms < e.locked_until {
            return Verdict::Limited {
                retry_after_s: ((e.locked_until - now_ms) as u64).div_ceil(1000).max(1),
            };
        }
        let dt = (now_ms - e.last_ms).max(0) as f64 / 1000.0;
        e.tokens = (e.tokens + dt * refill).min(capacity);
        e.last_ms = now_ms.max(e.last_ms);
        if e.tokens >= 1.0 {
            e.tokens -= 1.0;
            Verdict::Allow
        } else {
            let need = (1.0 - e.tokens) / refill.max(0.001);
            Verdict::Limited {
                retry_after_s: need.ceil().max(1.0) as u64,
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn record_failure(&mut self, ip: IpAddr, now_ms: i64) {
        let (limit, window, lockout) = (self.cfg.fail_limit, self.cfg.fail_window_ms, self.cfg.lockout_ms);
        let e = self.entry(ip, now_ms);
        e.fails.retain(|t| now_ms - *t < window);
        e.fails.push(now_ms);
        if e.fails.len() >= limit {
            e.fails.clear();
            e.locked_until = now_ms + lockout;

    }

        let mut rng = SplitMix64::new(0x4C34);
        for case in 0..300 {
            let mut l = Limiter::new(LimitConfig {
                max_addrs: 4,
                ..LimitConfig::default()

            let cfg = LimitConfig {
                capacity: (1 + rng.below(20)) as f64,
                refill_per_s: (1 + rng.below(30)) as f64,

//! Read-only LAN dashboard (PRD R22, architecture D6, safety rule 15).
//!
//! An axum server that serves the built frontend, a snapshot, a decimated trend
//! and a WebSocket stream of the sample bus to browsers on one private interface.
//! Off by default; a new self-signed certificate and token per start; GET only.
//! Nothing in this module can write to a device: it holds a [`LanSource`] that
//! can only read, and an [`AssetSource`] for static files.

pub mod hub;
pub mod limits;
pub mod net;
pub mod routes;
mod serve;
pub mod tls;
pub mod token;

use crate::profile::Profile;
use crate::session::{LiveSnapshot, Session};
use crate::trend::TrendSeries;
use limits::{LimitConfig, Limiter};
use net::{BindError, QrMatrix};
use routes::{ClientInfo, Ctx, Stats};
use serde::Serialize;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::net::{IpAddr, SocketAddr};
use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use tokio::sync::watch;
use tokio::task::JoinHandle;

pub use routes::ROUTES;

#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum LanError {
    #[error(transparent)]
    Bind(#[from] BindError),
    #[error("could not listen on {0}: {1}")]
    Listen(SocketAddr, String),
    #[error(transparent)]
    Tls(#[from] tls::TlsError),
    #[error("the operating system random source failed")]
    Random,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TrendFail {
    NotFound,
    Unavailable,
}

/// Everything the server may read. There is deliberately no method that writes.
pub trait LanSource: Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn subscribe(&self) -> BusSubscriber;
    fn snapshot(&self) -> LiveSnapshot;
    fn profiles(&self) -> Vec<Arc<Profile>>;
    fn trend(
        &self,
        device: &str,
        tag: &str,
        from_ms: i64,
        to_ms: i64,
        buckets: usize,
    ) -> Result<TrendSeries, TrendFail>;
}

impl LanSource for Session {
    fn subscribe(&self) -> BusSubscriber {
        Session::subscribe(self)
    }

    fn snapshot(&self) -> LiveSnapshot {
        Session::snapshot(self)
    }

    fn profiles(&self) -> Vec<Arc<Profile>> {
        Session::profiles(self)
    }

    fn trend(
        &self,
        device: &str,
        tag: &str,
        from_ms: i64,
        to_ms: i64,
        buckets: usize,
    ) -> Result<TrendSeries, TrendFail> {
        use crate::session::SessionError;
        Session::trend(self, device, tag, from_ms, to_ms, buckets).map_err(|e| match e {
            SessionError::UnknownDevice(_) => TrendFail::NotFound,
            _ => TrendFail::Unavailable,
        })
    }
}

pub struct Asset {
    pub mime: String,
    pub bytes: Vec<u8>,
}

pub trait AssetSource: Send + Sync + 'static {

/// Fixed in-memory files; used by tests.

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct LanConfig {
    pub ip: IpAddr,
    pub port: u16,
    /// Tests and the e2e build only; the UI never offers loopback.
    pub allow_loopback: bool,
    pub max_connections: usize,
    pub max_clients: usize,

impl LanConfig {
    pub fn new(ip: IpAddr, port: u16) -> Self {
        Self {
            ip,
            port,
            allow_loopback: false,
            max_connections: 32,
            max_clients: 8,

        }

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize)]
pub struct LanDetails {
    pub ip: String,
    pub port: u16,
    /// Contains the token: show it on the host device only.
    pub url: String,
    pub fingerprint: String,
    pub started_ms: i64,
    pub clients: Vec<ClientInfo>,
    pub max_clients: usize,
    pub max_connections: usize,
    pub rejected: u64,
    pub rate_limited: u64,
    pub refused_connections: u64,
    pub refused_clients: u64,
    pub qr: Option<QrMatrix>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize)]
pub struct LanStatus {
    pub running: bool,
    pub details: Option<LanDetails>,
}

impl LanStatus {
    pub fn off() -> Self {
        Self {
            running: false,
            details: None,
        }
    }
}

pub struct LanServer {
    addr: SocketAddr,
    token: String,
    fingerprint: String,
    started_ms: i64,
    cfg: LanConfig,
    ctx: Arc<Ctx>,
    hub: Arc<hub::Hub>,
    shutdown: watch::Sender<bool>,
    task: Option<JoinHandle<()>>,
}

fn now_ms() -> i64 {
    std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| i64::try_from(d.as_millis()).unwrap_or(i64::MAX))
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

impl LanServer {
    /// Bind, create a fresh certificate and token, and start serving.
    pub async fn start(
        cfg: LanConfig,
        source: Arc<dyn LanSource>,
        assets: Arc<dyn AssetSource>,
    ) -> Result<LanServer, LanError> {
        let want = net::check_bind(cfg.ip, cfg.port, cfg.allow_loopback)?;
        let token=<redacted>        let started_ms = now_ms();
        let cert = tls::generate(cfg.ip, started_ms)?;
        let acceptor = TlsAcceptor::from(tls::server_config(&cert)?);
        let listener = TcpListener::bind(want)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| LanError::Listen(want, e.to_string()))?;
        let addr = listener
            .local_addr()
            .map_err(|e| LanError::Listen(want, e.to_string()))?;
        let (shutdown, shutdown_rx) = watch::channel(false);
        let hub = hub::Hub::start(Arc::clone(&source));
        let ctx = Arc::new(Ctx {
            token=<redacted>,
            host_port: addr.to_string(),
            source,
            assets,
            hub: Arc::clone(&hub),
            limiter: Mutex::new(Limiter::new(cfg.limits)),
            clients: Mutex::new((0, Default::default())),
            max_clients: cfg.max_clients,
            stats: Stats::default(),
            shutdown: shutdown_rx.clone(),
            epoch: std::time::Instant::now(),
            epoch_ms: started_ms,
        });
        let task = tokio::spawn(serve::run(
            listener,
            acceptor,
            Arc::clone(&ctx),
            cfg.max_connections,
            shutdown_rx,
        ));
        Ok(LanServer {
            addr,
            token,
            fingerprint: cert.fingerprint,
            started_ms,
            cfg,
            ctx,
            hub,
            shutdown,
            task: Some(task),
        })
    }

    pub fn addr(&self) -> SocketAddr {
        self.addr
    }

    pub fn token(&self) -> &str {
        &self.token
    }

    pub fn fingerprint(&self) -> &str {
        &self.fingerprint
    }

    pub fn url(&self) -> String {
        format!("https://{}:{}/?t={}", self.addr.ip(), self.addr.port(), self.token)
    }

    pub fn status(&self) -> LanStatus {
        let s = &self.ctx.stats;
        let url = self.url();
        LanStatus {
            running: true,
            details: Some(LanDetails {
                ip: self.addr.ip().to_string(),
                port: self.addr.port(),
                qr: net::qr_matrix(&url),
                url,
                fingerprint: self.fingerprint.clone(),
                started_ms: self.started_ms,
                clients: self.ctx.client_list(),
                max_clients: self.cfg.max_clients,
                max_connections: self.cfg.max_connections,
                rejected: s.rejected.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
                rate_limited: s.limited.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
                refused_connections: s.refused_connections.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
                refused_clients: s.refused_clients.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            }),
        }
    }

    /// Close the listener and every connection, then forget the token and certificate.
    /// The port is free when this returns.
    pub async fn stop(mut self) {
        self.shutdown_now().await;
    }

    async fn shutdown_now(&mut self) {
        let _ = self.shutdown.send(true);
        if let Some(t) = self.task.take() {
            let _ = t.await;
        }
        let hub = Arc::clone(&self.hub);
        // The hub thread sleeps in 20 ms steps; join it off the async worker.
        let _ = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || hub.stop()).await;
    }
}

impl Drop for LanServer {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = self.shutdown.send(true);
        if let Some(t) = self.task.take() {
            t.abort();
        }
        self.hub.stop();
    }
}

            epoch: std::time::Instant::now(),

            listener,

            started_ms,

            ctx,
            hub,
            shutdown,

    pub fn addr(&self) -> SocketAddr {
        self.addr
    }

    pub fn token(&self) -> &str {
        &self.token
    }

    pub fn fingerprint(&self) -> &str {
        &self.fingerprint
    }

    pub fn status(&self) -> LanStatus {
        let s = &self.ctx.stats;
        let url = self.url();

            running: true,
            details: Some(LanDetails {
                ip: self.addr.ip().to_string(),
                port: self.addr.port(),
                qr: net::qr_matrix(&url),
                url,
                fingerprint: self.fingerprint.clone(),
                started_ms: self.started_ms,
                clients: self.ctx.client_list(),
                max_clients: self.cfg.max_clients,
                max_connections: self.cfg.max_connections,
                rejected: s.rejected.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
                rate_limited: s.limited.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
                refused_connections: s.refused_connections.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
                refused_clients: s.refused_clients.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            }),
        }
    }

    /// Close the listener and every connection, then forget the token and certificate.
    /// The port is free when this returns.
    pub async fn stop(mut self) {
        self.shutdown_now().await;
    }

    async fn shutdown_now(&mut self) {
        let _ = self.shutdown.send(true);
        if let Some(t) = self.task.take() {
            let _ = t.await;
        }
        let hub = Arc::clone(&self.hub);
        // The hub thread sleeps in 20 ms steps; join it off the async worker.
        let _ = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || hub.stop()).await;
    }
}

    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = self.shutdown.send(true);
        if let Some(t) = self.task.take() {
            t.abort();
        }
        self.hub.stop();
    }
}

//! Per-session self-signed certificate (rcgen) and the rustls server config.
//! The key never leaves memory: it lives in the server value and is dropped on stop.

use rcgen::{
    CertificateParams, DnType, ExtendedKeyUsagePurpose, IsCa, KeyPair, KeyUsagePurpose, SanType, date_time_ymd,
};
use rustls::ServerConfig;
use rustls::pki_types::{CertificateDer, PrivateKeyDer, PrivatePkcs8KeyDer};
use std::net::IpAddr;
use std::sync::Arc;
use thiserror::Error;

/// Validity of a session certificate.
pub const VALID_DAYS: i64 = 30;

#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum TlsError {
    #[error("could not create the certificate: {0}")]
    Cert(String),
    #[error("could not build the TLS configuration: {0}")]
    Config(String),
}

pub struct SessionCert {
    pub cert: CertificateDer<'static>,
    key: Vec<u8>,
    /// SHA-256 of the DER certificate, `AA:BB:…`.
    pub fingerprint: String,
}

/// Civil date (year, month, day) of a day count since 1970-01-01 (Howard Hinnant's algorithm).
pub fn civil_from_days(days: i64) -> (i32, u8, u8) {
    let z = days + 719_468;
    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    let doe = z.rem_euclid(146_097);
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let y = yoe + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let y = if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y };
    (y as i32, m as u8, d as u8)
}

pub fn fingerprint(der: &[u8]) -> String {
    let d = ring::digest::digest(&ring::digest::SHA256, der);
    d.as_ref()
        .iter()
        .map(|b| format!("{b:02X}"))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(":")
}

pub fn generate(ip: IpAddr, now_ms: i64) -> Result<SessionCert, TlsError> {
    let mut params = CertificateParams::new(Vec::<String>::new()).map_err(|e| TlsError::Cert(e.to_string()))?;
    params.subject_alt_names = vec![SanType::IpAddress(ip)];
    params
        .distinguished_name
        .push(DnType::CommonName, "BusLink Studio LAN view");
    params.is_ca = IsCa::NoCa;
    params.key_usages = vec![KeyUsagePurpose::DigitalSignature];
    params.extended_key_usages = vec![ExtendedKeyUsagePurpose::ServerAuth];
    let date = |plus_days: i64| {
        let (y, m, d) = civil_from_days(now_ms.div_euclid(86_400_000) + plus_days);
        date_time_ymd(y, m, d)
    };
    params.not_before = date(-1);
    params.not_after = date(VALID_DAYS);
    let key = KeyPair::generate().map_err(|e| TlsError::Cert(e.to_string()))?;
    let cert = params.self_signed(&key).map_err(|e| TlsError::Cert(e.to_string()))?;
    let der = cert.der().clone();
    Ok(SessionCert {
        fingerprint: fingerprint(der.as_ref()),
        cert: der,
        key: key.serialize_der(),
    })
}

pub fn server_config(c: &SessionCert) -> Result<Arc<ServerConfig>, TlsError> {
    let provider = Arc::new(rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider());
    let key = PrivateKeyDer::Pkcs8(PrivatePkcs8KeyDer::from(c.key.clone()));
    let mut cfg = ServerConfig::builder_with_provider(provider)
        .with_safe_default_protocol_versions()
        .map_err(|e| TlsError::Config(e.to_string()))?
        .with_no_client_auth()
        .with_single_cert(vec![c.cert.clone()], key)
        .map_err(|e| TlsError::Config(e.to_string()))?;
    cfg.alpn_protocols = vec![b"http/1.1".to_vec()];
    Ok(Arc::new(cfg))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn civil_dates() {
        assert_eq!(civil_from_days(0), (1970, 1, 1));
        assert_eq!(civil_from_days(19_723), (2024, 1, 1));
        assert_eq!(civil_from_days(20_513), (2026, 3, 1));
        assert_eq!(civil_from_days(-1), (1969, 12, 31));
    }

    #[test]
    fn certificates_differ_per_session_and_config_builds() {
        let ip: IpAddr = "192.168.1.20".parse().unwrap();
        let a = generate(ip, 1_800_000_000_000).unwrap();
        let b = generate(ip, 1_800_000_000_000).unwrap();
        assert_ne!(a.fingerprint, b.fingerprint);
        assert_eq!(a.fingerprint.len(), 32 * 2 + 31);
        server_config(&a).unwrap();
    }
}

//! IPC for the LAN dashboard and MQTT telemetry (lan-mqtt design §5).
//!
//! Both are off at every start. Nothing here carries a frame, an address or a
//! function code, and nothing here writes to a device. The MQTT password goes to
//! the secret store only; it is never saved in a file, logged or returned.

use crate::state::AppState;
use buslink_core::lan::net::{self, DEFAULT_PORT, Interface};
use buslink_core::lan::{Asset, AssetSource, LanConfig, LanServer, LanStatus};
#[cfg(not(windows))]
use buslink_core::mqtt::MemorySecretStore;
use buslink_core::mqtt::{MqttConfig, MqttInit, MqttService, MqttStatus, Secret, SecretStore, TestReport, random_client_id, test_connection};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::net::{IpAddr, Ipv4Addr};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;
use tauri::async_runtime::Mutex;
use tauri::{AppHandle, Manager, State};

type R<T> = Result<T, String>;

const PASSWORD_KEY: &str = "mqtt-password";
const CONFIG_FILE: &str = "mqtt.json";
const OUTBOX_FILE: &str = "buslink-mqtt-outbox.sqlite3";
#[cfg(windows)]
const KEYRING_SERVICE: &str = "id.co.arkamaya.buslink";

/// Static files of the frontend build, from the Tauri asset resolver (the same files the window shows).
struct TauriAssets(AppHandle);

impl AssetSource for TauriAssets {
    fn get(&self, path: &str) -> Option<Asset> {
        let a = self.0.asset_resolver().get(path.to_string())?;
        // The resolver answers unknown paths with index.html (SPA fallback). Only `index.html`
        // itself may be HTML here, so an unknown path stays a 404.
        if a.mime_type.starts_with("text/html") && path != "index.html" {
            return None;
        }
        Some(Asset {
            mime: a.mime_type,
            bytes: a.bytes,
        })
    }
}

/// Windows Credential Manager.
#[cfg(windows)]
struct WindowsSecrets;

#[cfg(windows)]
impl SecretStore for WindowsSecrets {
    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Result<Option<Secret>, buslink_core::mqtt::secrets::SecretError> {
        use buslink_core::mqtt::secrets::SecretError;
        let e = keyring::Entry::new(KEYRING_SERVICE, key).map_err(|e| SecretError(e.to_string()))?;
        match e.get_password() {
            Ok(p) => Ok(Some(Secret=<redacted>,
            Err(keyring::Error::NoEntry) => Ok(None),
            Err(e) => Err(SecretError(e.to_string())),
        }
    }

    fn set(&self, key: &str, value: &Secret) -> Result<(), buslink_core::mqtt::secrets::SecretError> {
        use buslink_core::mqtt::secrets::SecretError;
        keyring::Entry::new(KEYRING_SERVICE, key)
            .and_then(|e| e.set_password(value.expose()))
            .map_err(|e| SecretError(e.to_string()))
    }

    fn delete(&self, key: &str) -> Result<(), buslink_core::mqtt::secrets::SecretError> {
        use buslink_core::mqtt::secrets::SecretError;
        match keyring::Entry::new(KEYRING_SERVICE, key).and_then(|e| e.delete_credential()) {
            Ok(()) | Err(keyring::Error::NoEntry) => Ok(()),
            Err(e) => Err(SecretError(e.to_string())),
        }
    }

    fn kind(&self) -> &'static str {
        "windows-credential-manager"
    }

    fn persistent(&self) -> bool {
        true
    }
}

/// Windows Credential Manager on Windows; memory only elsewhere (Android Keystore is not wired yet).
pub fn secret_store() -> Arc<dyn SecretStore> {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        Arc::new(WindowsSecrets)
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        Arc::new(MemorySecretStore::default())
    }
}

/// What the Share and MQTT panels need besides the Core state.
pub struct ShareState {
    lan: Mutex<Option<LanServer>>,
    mqtt: Mutex<Option<MqttService>>,
    secrets: Arc<dyn SecretStore>,
}

impl ShareState {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            lan: Mutex::new(None),
            mqtt: Mutex::new(None),
            secrets: secret_store(),
        }
    }

    /// Close sharing and MQTT (app exit). Blocking; called from the exit handler.
    pub fn shutdown(&self) {
        tauri::async_runtime::block_on(async {
            if let Some(s) = self.lan.lock().await.take() {
                s.stop().await;
            }
            if let Some(m) = self.mqtt.lock().await.take() {
                m.stop().await;
            }
        });

//! MQTT settings that may be saved to a file. There is no password field, and
//! unknown keys are an error, so a hand-edited `"password"` is refused, not read.

use super::topic::sanitize_level;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use thiserror::Error;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct MqttConfig {
    /// `mqtts://host[:8883]`; `mqtt://host[:1883]` only with `allow_insecure`.
    pub broker_url: String,
    pub site: String,
    pub gateway: String,
    pub client_id: String,
    /// Empty = anonymous. The password lives in the secret=<redacted>    pub username: String,
    /// Extra CA certificate(s) in PEM for a private broker.
    pub ca_pem: String,
    pub allow_insecure: bool,
    pub expiry_s: u32,
    pub keep_alive_s: u16,
    pub outbox_max: usize,
    pub min_interval_ms: u64,
}

impl Default for MqttConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            broker_url: String::new(),
            site: "site1".into(),
            gateway: "gateway1".into(),
            client_id: "buslink".into(),
            username: String::new(),
            ca_pem: String::new(),
            allow_insecure: false,
            expiry_s: 3600,
            keep_alive_s: 30,
            outbox_max: 10_000,
            min_interval_ms: 1000,
        }
    }
}

/// `buslink-` plus 4 random bytes as hex.
pub fn random_client_id() -> String {
    use ring::rand::{SecureRandom, SystemRandom};
    let mut b = [0u8; 4];
    match SystemRandom::new().fill(&mut b) {
        Ok(()) => format!("buslink-{}", crate::lan::token=<redacted>,
        Err(_) => "buslink".into(),
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Broker {
    pub host: String,
    pub port: u16,
    pub tls: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Error, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ConfigError {
    #[error("broker URL: {0}")]
    Url(String),
    #[error("{field}: {message}")]
    Field { field: &'static str, message: String },
}

fn field(field: &'static str, message: impl Into<String>) -> ConfigError {
    ConfigError::Field {
        field,
        message: message.into(),
    }
}

impl MqttConfig {
    /// Check every field and return the parsed broker address.
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<Broker, ConfigError> {
        let broker = parse_broker(&self.broker_url, self.allow_insecure)?;
        if self.site.trim().is_empty() {
            return Err(field("site", "must not be empty"));
        }
        if self.gateway.trim().is_empty() {
            return Err(field("gateway", "must not be empty"));
        }
        let id = &self.client_id;
        if id.is_empty() || id.len() > 64 || !id.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '-' || c == '_') {
            return Err(field("client_id", "1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, - and _"));
        }
        if self.username.len() > 128 || self.username.chars().any(char::is_control) {
            return Err(field("username", "at most 128 characters, no control characters"));
        }
        if !(1..=7 * 86_400).contains(&self.expiry_s) {
            return Err(field("expiry_s", "1 s to 7 days"));
        }
        if !(5..=1200).contains(&self.keep_alive_s) {
            return Err(field("keep_alive_s", "5 s to 1200 s"));
        }
        if !(100..=1_000_000).contains(&self.outbox_max) {
            return Err(field("outbox_max", "100 to 1 000 000 messages"));
        }
        if self.min_interval_ms > 3_600_000 {
            return Err(field("min_interval_ms", "at most 1 hour"));
        }
        if !self.ca_pem.is_empty() && (self.ca_pem.len() > 65_536 || !self.ca_pem.contains("BEGIN CERTIFICATE")) {
            return Err(field(
                "ca_pem",
                "must be a PEM certificate (BEGIN CERTIFICATE), at most 64 KB",
            ));
        }

//! Certificate verification for the broker connection (research/03 rows 56–57).
//!
//! Desktop: the operating system's roots (`rustls-native-certs`) plus an optional
//! user CA. Android: `rustls-platform-verifier` (needs its Kotlin component, see
//! docs/android-build.md); with a user CA the connection trusts only that CA.

use super::MqttError;
use rustls::ClientConfig;
use rustls::RootCertStore;
use rustls::pki_types::CertificateDer;
use rustls::pki_types::pem::PemObject;
use std::sync::Arc;

fn provider() -> Arc<rustls::crypto::CryptoProvider> {
    Arc::new(rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider())
}

pub fn parse_pem(pem: &str) -> Result<Vec<CertificateDer<'static>>, MqttError> {
    if pem.trim().is_empty() {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    }
    let certs: Vec<CertificateDer<'static>> = CertificateDer::pem_slice_iter(pem.as_bytes())
        .collect::<Result<_, _>>()
        .map_err(|e| MqttError::Tls(format!("the CA PEM could not be read: {e}")))?;
    if certs.is_empty() {
        return Err(MqttError::Tls("the CA PEM contains no certificate".into()));
    }
    Ok(certs)
}

fn tls_err(e: rustls::Error) -> MqttError {
    MqttError::Tls(e.to_string())
}

/// Roots made only of the user's CA (private broker).
fn user_roots(extra: Vec<CertificateDer<'static>>) -> Result<RootCertStore, MqttError> {
    let mut roots = RootCertStore::empty();
    for c in extra {
        roots
            .add(c)
            .map_err(|e| MqttError::Tls(format!("the CA certificate is not usable: {e}")))?;
    }
    Ok(roots)
}

#[cfg(not(target_os = "android"))]
pub fn client_config(extra_ca_pem: &str) -> Result<Arc<ClientConfig>, MqttError> {
    let extra = parse_pem(extra_ca_pem)?;
    let mut roots = user_roots(extra)?;
    let native = rustls_native_certs::load_native_certs();
    for c in native.certs {
        // A few platform roots can be unparsable; skip them rather than fail.
        let _ = roots.add(c);
    }
    if roots.is_empty() {
        return Err(MqttError::Tls(
            "no trusted root certificates were found on this system; add a CA certificate".into(),
        ));
    }
    let cfg = ClientConfig::builder_with_provider(provider())
        .with_safe_default_protocol_versions()
        .map_err(tls_err)?
        .with_root_certificates(roots)
        .with_no_client_auth();
    Ok(Arc::new(cfg))
}

#[cfg(target_os = "android")]
pub fn client_config(extra_ca_pem: &str) -> Result<Arc<ClientConfig>, MqttError> {
    use rustls_platform_verifier::BuilderVerifierExt;
    let extra = parse_pem(extra_ca_pem)?;
    let builder = ClientConfig::builder_with_provider(provider())
        .with_safe_default_protocol_versions()
        .map_err(tls_err)?;
    let cfg = if extra.is_empty() {
        builder.with_platform_verifier().map_err(tls_err)?.with_no_client_auth()
    } else {
        builder.with_root_certificates(user_roots(extra)?).with_no_client_auth()
    };
    Ok(Arc::new(cfg))
}

package id.co.arkamaya.buslink.usb

import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap

/**
 * Process-wide USB state shared by the plugin and the foreground service.
 * Nothing here persists: a new process starts with no open port and no service
 * (reattach or restart never resumes polling, safety rule 6).
 */
object UsbRuntime {
    /** Open ports by port ID. One owner per port: a second open is refused. */
    val sessions = ConcurrentHashMap<String, SerialSession>()

    @Volatile var lastEvent: String? = null
    @Volatile var serviceRunning: Boolean = false
    @Volatile var serviceError: String? = null

    fun event(text: String) {
        lastEvent = text
    }

    fun closeAll(reason: String) {
        val all = sessions.values.toList()
        sessions.clear()
        for (s in all) s.close(EndState.CLOSED)
        if (all.isNotEmpty()) event(reason)
    }

    /** The adapter with this device node was unplugged. */
    fun detached(deviceName: String) {
        val hit = sessions.values.filter { it.deviceName == deviceName }
        for (s in hit) {
            sessions.remove(s.portId)
            s.close(EndState.DETACHED)
        }
        if (hit.isNotEmpty()) {
            event("USB adapter detached: $deviceName")
            PollingService.instance?.stopSelf()
        }
    }
}

pub struct ConnectReq {
    /// `rtu`, `tcp` or `rtu_over_tcp`
    kind: String,
    port: Option<String>,
    baud: Option<u32>,
    data_bits: Option<u8>,
    parity: Option<Parity>,
    stop_bits: Option<u8>,
    host: Option<String>,
    tcp_port: Option<u16>,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct ConnectResult {
    link_id: String,
    /// RTU links show the non-isolated adapter advice (safety rule 18).
    isolation_advice: bool,
    /// Android RTU over OTG: the phone usually cannot charge, mind the battery (safety rule 18).
    otg_battery_advice: bool,
    /// Android: baud above 115 200 can lose fragments (research/03 row 37).
    high_baud_warning: bool,

/// What Start polling achieved beyond polling itself (android-otg Req 6.7).
#[derive(Serialize, Default)]
pub struct StartResult {
    android: bool,
    /// The foreground service runs, so polling continues with the screen off.
    background: bool,
    notifications_denied: bool,
    error: Option<String>,
}

fn slug(s: &str) -> String {
    let out: String = s
        .chars()
        .map(|c| {
            if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
                c.to_ascii_lowercase()
            } else {
                '-'
            }
        })
        .collect();
    out.trim_matches('-').chars().take(40).collect()
}

fn serial_of(r: &ConnectReq) -> R<SerialSettings> {
    let s = SerialSettings::new(
        r.baud.unwrap_or(9600),
        r.data_bits.unwrap_or(8),
        r.parity.unwrap_or(Parity::None),
        r.stop_bits.unwrap_or(1),
    );
    s.validate().map_err(str::to_owned)?;
    Ok(s)
}

fn host_of(r: &ConnectReq) -> R<(String, u16)> {
    let host = r.host.as_deref().map(str::trim).unwrap_or_default();
    let ok = !host.is_empty()
        && host.len() <= 253
        && host
            .chars()
            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '.' | '-' | ':' | '[' | ']'));
    if !ok {
        return Err("host must be an IP address or host name".into());
    }
    let port = r.tcp_port.unwrap_or(502);
    if port == 0 {
        return Err("TCP port must be 1-65535".into());
    }
    Ok((host.to_owned(), port))
}

#[tauri::command]
pub async fn connect_link(state: State<'_, AppState>, req: ConnectReq) -> R<ConnectResult> {
    // Opening a USB port may show the Android permission dialog and wait for the
    // answer, which arrives on the main thread: run off it.
    let session = Arc::clone(&state.session);
    tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking(move || connect_blocking(&session, req))
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
}

fn connect_blocking(session: &Session, req: ConnectReq) -> R<ConnectResult> {
    let android = cfg!(target_os = "android");
    let mut high_baud_warning = false;
    let (config, rtu) = match req.kind.as_str() {
        "rtu" => {
            let port = req.port.clone().unwrap_or_default();
            if port.trim().is_empty() || port.len() > 64 {
                return Err("choose a serial port".into());
            }
            let serial = serial_of(&req)?;
            high_baud_warning = android && serial.baud > crate::android_usb::MAX_RELIABLE_BAUD;
            (
                LinkConfig {
                    id: slug(&port),
                    kind: LinkKind::Rtu { port, serial },
                    // Android USB-serial needs at least 50 ms between frames (modbus.md).
                    min_inter_frame_ms: if android { 50 } else { 0 },
                },
                true,
            )
        }
        "tcp" => {
            let (host, port) = host_of(&req)?;
            (
                LinkConfig {
                    id: format!("tcp-{}-{port}", slug(&host)),
                    kind: LinkKind::Tcp { host, port },
                    min_inter_frame_ms: 0,
                },
                false,
            )
        }
        "rtu_over_tcp" => {
            let (host, port) = host_of(&req)?;
            let serial = serial_of(&req)?;
            (
                LinkConfig {
                    id: format!("rtutcp-{}-{port}", slug(&host)),
                    kind: LinkKind::RtuOverTcp { host, port, serial },
                    min_inter_frame_ms: 0,
                },
                false,
            )
        }
        _ => return Err("unknown link kind".into()),
    };
    let link_id = config.id.clone();
    session.connect(config, false).map_err(err)?;
    Ok(ConnectResult {
        link_id,
        isolation_advice: rtu,
        otg_battery_advice: android && rtu,
        high_baud_warning,
    })
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn reconnect_link(state: State<'_, AppState>, id: String) -> R<()> {
    state.session.reconnect(&id).map_err(err)
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn disconnect_link(state: State<'_, AppState>, id: String) -> R<()> {
    state.session.disconnect(&id).map_err(err)
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn remove_link(state: State<'_, AppState>, id: String) -> R<()> {
    state.session.remove_link(&id).map_err(err)
}

## Verdict per category

1. **Write frames outside `command/` and the simulator: no findings.** FC05/06/15/16 constants and encoding exist only in `command/wire.rs`. The only other users of `WriteRequest` are the simulator (decoding) and `command/mod.rs`. Tauri IPC carries only device, command and register IDs plus engineering values (`PanelRequest` uses `deny_unknown_fields`). There is no raw-PDU endpoint and no write method on `LanSource`.
2. **Command service bypass: no findings.**
   - `execute` requires the `Confirmed` state, and `ensure_armed` re-checks expiry at preview, confirm and execute.
   - `PreparedFrame` is not `Clone` and is consumed by `send`.
   - A second `execute` fails with `WrongState`.
   - Unit 0 gives `BroadcastRejected`, and the unit is range-checked against the link.
   - If the audit write fails, nothing is sent (fail-closed). Link loss disarms.
   - No retry exists anywhere in the module.
   - Reconnect, profile change and disconnect all disarm.
   - The exception is the self-asserted role above.
3. **Bounds: no findings.**
   - `check_bounds` rejects, never clamps.
   - It handles `allowed_values`, `min`/`max`, `step` and `valid_range`, rejects non-finite values, and refuses writes when no bounds exist.
   - The profile validator requires `step > 0`, which closes the NaN pass-through I suspected.
   - Comm-config values are checked: unit ID 1–247, and baud must be in the profile's code table.
   - Comm registers cannot be written outside the wizard.
4. **LAN server: no findings beyond the low items above.**
   - The guard middleware wraps every route and the fallback.
   - Order is rate limit, token, body rejection, GET-only.
   - The token is 128 bits from the OS random source, compared with `ct_eq`.
   - Bind is private IPv4 only (`check_bind` refuses `0.0.0.0`, IPv6, public and multicast), the port is ≥1024, and the server is off by default.
   - Each start gets a fresh rcgen certificate and token. Stop drops the token and key and joins the tasks.
   - There are limits on rate, failures with lockout, connections, WebSocket clients, message size and handshake time.
   - I found no logging of the token. The cookie is `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`. The WebSocket origin is checked, there is no CORS, and path traversal is blocked.
5. **MQTT: no findings.**
   - The config has no password field and rejects unknown keys.
   - The password lives in Windows Credential Manager (memory-only elsewhere), and errors go through `redact`.
   - TLS is the default. Plain `mqtt://` needs an explicit `allow_insecure`. Credentials in the URL are refused.
   - Verification uses native roots (or the platform verifier on Android) plus an optional user CA.
   - A search of non-test code found no verifier bypass. The only `dangerous()` use is a pinning client in test code.
   - There are no subscriptions.
   - The outbox is capped at 100–1M rows and holds telemetry only.
6. **Profiles, imports, exports: no findings, with limits on what I checked.** Profile JSON has a 1 MB cap, duplicate-key rejection, `deny_unknown_fields`, and no expression evaluation. `guard_text` escapes `= + - @`, tab and CR, and is used in CSV and XLSX (strings are written with `write_string`). Quality and exception columns are present in every export. I did not find the `.mbmap` or CSV import code, so I could not check its size limits.
7. **Android: no findings, partly verified.**
   - **Verified:**
     - The service is `exported="false"` with type `connectedDevice`.
     - The permission set matches the rules (no storage permissions).
     - The permission request uses an explicit package intent, a 60 s timeout, a request ID extra, and a `RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED` detach receiver.
     - `onStop` cancels the pending request.
     - SAF export uses `ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT` with a safe-name regex and a MIME allow-list.
     - The FileProvider is not exported.
   - **Not checked:**
     - The PendingIntent flags (`FLAG_MUTABLE | FLAG_CANCEL_CURRENT`) beyond seeing the call.
     - The sender and request-ID match in `onReceive`.
     - `onDestroy` cancellation.
     - That the foreground service is started only from the foreground after the grant.
     - Partial-document deletion.
8. **Tauri: no findings.** The capability is `core:default` only, with no shell, fs, http or dialog grants for the webview. The CSP is set, with `connect-src` limited to IPC and `frame-ancestors 'none'`. No remote content is loaded. Input is validated: connect settings, `lan_start` (the IP must be one of the machine's listed interfaces) and `report_save_html` (5 MB cap plus a doctype check).
9. **Secrets: no findings.** A regex scan for private keys, AWS and GitHub tokens, and hard-coded password, token or secret=<redacted> over source and config files found nothing. `.gitleaks.toml` exists. I did not scan git history or binary files.
10. **Quality honesty: no findings in the code I read, but not fully verified.** Exports, MQTT payloads and the LAN stream carry quality and age. MQTT replays the original `ts` and `seq`, and the LAN `lagged` path resends a full snapshot instead of skipping.
